messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: SLO alert - streaming /v1/chat/stream p95 and p99 exceed thresholds in us-west-2. automated detection at 2026-03-15T09:12:25Z

maria: acked the page, I'm oncall for today. looking at dashboard now. any customer-facing errors? :phone:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-3283. Severity: high. Paging maria, alex.

alex: seeing a sharp jump in tail latency for streaming shards. p95 -> 1.1s (baseline ~120ms), p99 -> 5.6s. tokenization preproc queue depth spiked.

samir: logs show a burst of large JSON-mode prompts hitting prompt-builder v2. the template expander is doing recursive schema validation for tool schemas (big JSON blobs).

jess: attaching quick histogram from the last 15m:
```
p50: 90ms
p90: 220ms
p95: 1.1s
p99: 5.6s
max: 12.3s
```

maria: are streaming stalls observed (partial chunk sends) or just end-to-end latency?

alex: both. some streams are sending initial chunks then stalling ~3-8s mid-stream. looks like KV cache / batching handshake delay after tokenization.

emily-cs: we've had 2 customers open realtime tickets reporting slow replies and UI spinners. CS categorizes impact as degraded interactive experience (not total outage).

samir: correlating with deploys — there was a template-expander change rolled 09:05 (SHA b4c3). rollout 20% -> 100% by 09:08. spikes start ~09:10.

jess: stacktrace snippet from prompt-builder worker:
```
ERROR prompt_builder: expand_template() took 2312ms for schema length 42KB
  at template_expander.py:line 217
  at validator.py:line 89
  at tool_schema.py:line 130
```

maria: mitigation options? immediate: rollback template-expander, throttle JSON-mode routes, enable suffix/prefix caching, route streaming traffic to fallback smaller model. which is fastest?

alex: fastest low-risk: flip prefix cache on for the overloaded routes (config flag). second: throttle incoming JSON-mode to 10r/s via rate-limit middleware. rollback will take ~8-12min and requires canary.

samir: I can flip prefix cache and add rate-limit in the ingress layer now. doing prefix-cache: true on routes /v1/chat/stream high-latency pool. Command:
```
# toggle cache
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://ops-api/configs/routes/cache -d '{"route":"/v1/chat/stream","prefix_cache":true}'
```

maria: do it. also throttle JSON-mode: set header-based limit for content-type application/json+mode=tool-schema to 10r/s

samir: throttle applied. monitoring...

jess: after throttle + cache flip: p95 back to 240ms, p99 900ms within 3m. streaming stalls decreased.

emily-cs: telling affected customers we applied mitigation, investigating root cause. asking to hold on rollback unless needed.

alex: root cause hypothesis: the template-expander change introduced expensive schema validation path for JSON-mode tool schemas. it increased per-request CPU and introduced jitter in preproc queueing that cascades into batching/kv handshake delays for streaming.

maria: agree. next steps: 1) revert template-expander PR and run canary against heavy JSON-mode traces 2) add micro-bench for schema lengths > 10KB to block on PRs 3) add circuit-breaker to bypass validation when backlog > X 4) postmortem owner = samir.

samir: taking postmortem. I'll open INC-2026-0315-3283-PM and assign timeline + remediation tasks.

jess: also recommend adding telemetry: per-route template-expansion duration tag + per-request tool-schema-size metric to alert before SLOs hit.

emily-cs: CS follow-up: we emailed the two affected customers, offered credits for degraded experience, and will share postmortem when complete.

maria: final note: mitigation kept customer-visible error rate low, no data loss. leaving the thread open for rollback decision if canary shows failures. great work, team. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-3283 acknowledged by maria. Current status: mitigated, monitoring.

maria: logging follow-up tasks in tracking board, will convert to blameless postmortem tomorrow. closing active paging for now.

alex: saved traces and pcap for 09:05-09:15 window in s3://rw-incidents/2026-03-15/4280012345/ for postmortem.

samir: thanks — will include perf repro and benchmark before re-rolling.

emily-cs: closing customer-facing thread after PM published.
